chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Taking a steady job with Great American Insurance
summary: Because music wasn't steady he took an easy insurance job starting at noon, staying eighteen years until the company moved to California.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: This went on for several years, and then you decided to get yourself a steady day job.

Well, this went on, yes. And that was one of the reasons I did get a steady job -- because the music wasn't steady. So I was talking to the wife: "Well, now, you're getting along in age now. It's time to start thinking about your old age." One of them kind of things. I said, "Yeah, I guess so."

So I went to work for Great American Insurance Company. I had a nice, easy job there. What I liked about it, I didn't have to work until twelve o'clock in the day. So if I had any night gigs or things to play, I could still make them, and I didn't have to deal with anything. But I didn't think I would be on the job that long as I stayed there. I

stayed there eighteen years. And the only reason I left then was because they moved out to California. It was a nice eighteen years. If it was hard, I wouldn't have been there. I'm not the most diligent worker in the world.
